To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mixing efficiency of granulation liquid during continuous twin screw wet granulation can be significantly increased by increasing the moisture content and by optimizing the screw configuration.

(1) the residence time distribution of material inside the twin screw granulator is a function of screw speed, moisture content and the screw configuration, (2) a more uniform distribution of granulation solution is achieved with higher moisture content and more kneading zones, and (3) increasing the moisture content is the only process parameter that significantly improves the mixing of powder and liquid phase in continuous twin screw granulators.

the residence time of the material inside the barrel is dependent on the screw speed and moisture level, the granulation liquid is homogeneously mixed and evenly distributed inside the screw chamber at higher moisture levels, and the moisture content has a major effect on the mixing efficiency and the distribution of the granulation liquids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a continuous twin-screw granulation process for pharmaceutical drug formulations and the understanding of the liquid distribution and mixing inside the screw chamber.
the development of continuous granulation processes, which can be used for the production of high quality drug products with a high degree of process understanding.
the development of an in-line process monitoring and control tool that will enable the continuous manufacturing of pharmaceutical granules with a high quality and uniformity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the granulation liquid is not mixed homogeneously during continuous twin screw wet granulation, and that the mixing efficiency of granulation liquid is dependent on the screw configuration and the moisture content.
a continuous twin screw system is a very efficient mixer, but only at high moisture content and high screw speed.
increasing the moisture content is a more effective way to improve the mixing of the liquid and powder phases in a continuous twin screw wet granulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mixing of liquid and powder phase is not sufficient during continuous twin screw wet granulation, especially when the moisture content is low and the screw configuration is not optimized.
the mixing efficiency of liquid and powder material can be improved by increasing the screw speed and moisture level.
the residence time of the powder material inside the barrel and the granulation liquid homogeneity are both important parameters for the continuous twin screw granulator performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the moisture content is a critical parameter for ensuring a homogenous granulation liquid mixing in twin screw granulation.

the mixing of granulating liquid and dry powder is not as efficient in continuous twin screw granulators as in batch granulators, and therefore, the liquid distribution inside the granulator is a critical parameter that should be taken into account during process development.
the granulation liquid needs to be added in a controlled way to ensure homogenous mixing.
